newsitem.title: INDIA: New India shipping policy expected in a month.
newsitem.headline: New India shipping policy expected in a month.

text.p: India expects to announce a new shipping policy within a month, a senior civil servant in the country's surface transport ministry told Reuters on Thursday.
"I hope to have a report out very soon," Director-General of Shipping Michael Pinto told Reuters in an interview. "We hope it will come out within a month."
Pinto said the policy would cover major aspects of the import and financing regulations for the purchase of new vessels, which are widely expected to give a boost to India's shipping industry.
"We're trying to cover all the issues," he said in reply to a question. "We want to make sure that no issue, however slight, is not covered."

Indian shipowners say financial burdens imposed by taxes and high interest rates have handicapped them while freer competitors streamed into Indian ports hungry for a share of the growth in cargo that followed reforms begun in 1991.

The Indian National Shipowners' Association has pleaded for tax and duty reliefs and an annual allocation of $300 million for commercial borrowings for shipping. But it is still awaiting a response from the finance ministry.
